dataset_name: EPA TRI (Toxics Release Inventory) - PFAS chemicals
public_access: yes - no key; bulk download + Envirofacts
texas_coverage: not yet extracted (national: 61 facilities reported PFAS in RY2023, per EPA)
years_available: RY2020-present (172 PFAS added under NDAA; +9 more in 2023; +7 more from RY2024)
pfas_compounds: up to ~200 PFAS chemicals now reportable
sample_size: n/a - facility census (only facilities above reporting thresholds)
sampling_design: mandatory self-report by facilities meeting thresholds
temporal_compatibility_with_phase1: new window (RY2020+) vs UCMR5's 2023-2025 - partial overlap
spatial_compatibility_with_zcta_pws: facility point -> straightforward spatial join to ZCTA/buffer
exposure_pathway: source-pressure proxy (air/water/land release quantity), not ambient concentration
major_limitations: Only large qualifying facilities report; many diffuse/legacy sources (old AFFF use) are not captured; reporting thresholds may exclude smaller emitters
retain_decision: RETAIN (facility-level source-pressure layer for Direction B/C)

dataset_name: EPA National PFAS Analytic Tools / ECHO National PFAS Datasets (aggregator)
public_access: yes - no key; ECHO Data Downloads page has bulk files
years_available: varies by underlying source (bundles UCMR/state DW/CDR/WQP/NPDES-DMR/Superfund/Federal Sites/TRI/RCRA/AFFF spills/GHGRP - 12 categories total)
linkage_unit: facility or PWS ID depending on layer
spatial_compatibility_with_zcta_pws: facility/point layers -> spatial join; PWS layers -> same PWS linkage as Phase 1
exposure_pathway: multiple (drinking water + discharge + release + federal-site investigation)
major_limitations: A convenience aggregator, not a new primary source - but likely the single most efficient starting point for Direction B/C since it pre-bundles federal sites, TRI, Superfund and AFFF-spill data with a documented public metadata PDF
retain_decision: RETAIN (highest-priority next check - see decision log)
